THE RULE: in src/concordance/verifiers/base.py, a stated literal earns a window only when, read as a number the same way stated_precision reads it, it equals the value the claim states, up to float representation. window_for takes that claimed value as a required argument. Where they differ, the literal is ignored and the verifier compares as if none was given, so a true claim still reads and a false one reads BROKEN; the recorded data says the literal was not the claim's. The comparison is made in the claim's own unit, before any conversion. An unreadable literal earns nothing, as today. The hedged flag widens only a literal that passed this test.

EVERY CALLER: every reader of a stated literal goes through that test: window_for's callers in economics, finance, geometry, labor, mathematics, periodic_table, physical_constants, physics and units; stated_window's in mathematics' equality and in scale_base; chemistry's _matches_at_precision; astronomy's; and anything else the walk finds. An AST test walks src/concordance/verifiers and fails on any call of window_for without the claimed value, and on any reader of stated_window, stated_tolerance_abs or stated_precision not listed with its reason; audit.py's reads at extraction are listed, since they build the literal from the claim. It proves it can fail on a planted caller.

THE FLOAT EDGE: band() in base.py never counts a non-finite value as inside. A finite computed value against a claim that is not finite reads MISMATCH, which is proof the claim is false; a computed value that is not finite reads error, since that is could-not-compare, never a BROKEN. Physics' conservation and kinematic checks and every other band() caller inherit it, and a test holds both cases through a band() caller in at least three verifiers.

THE MEMO: src/concordance/bucket.py's fingerprint for every domain covers verifiers/base.py, and scale_base.py where a verifier reads through it, so a stored verdict does not outlive a change to the shared comparison. A test proves a changed copy moves the key for several domains, clearing _FINGERPRINTS, and that an old stored verdict is not served. The ship note states every domain's memo entries miss once after the ship and stay on disk unread.

ROWS: for each caller, a test holds a claim whose literal matches and is inside its window reading HOLDS; a false claim whose literal is its own reading BROKEN; and a false claim carrying a literal that is not its own reading BROKEN, through tools/benchmark.py's verify. The moat's own literal cases and every text extractor's claims keep their readings. A claim with a hedge reads as today when its literal is its own. Tests hold no false claim reading HOLDS.

NOTHING ELSE MOVES: the moat stays 1,796, 0 false positives, 0 false negatives; tools/restatement_audit.py exits 0 with MEASURED.md's numbers unchanged. Every reading that moves is named by verifier, and none moves toward HOLDS. The run changes only src/concordance/verifiers/, src/concordance/bucket.py, tests/, CHANGELOG.md and the run's ledger, and nothing under tools/, data/ or deploy/. New tests are in tests/MANIFEST.txt. Checker gates start with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE removed. No ledger event, commit message or report holds a working row.

goal: A claim's stated precision belongs to the claim. window_for and stated_window in verifiers/base.py widen a comparison from a literal written beside a claim, so a true claim stated to its precision reads HOLDS; that is right, and the text extractors build the literal from the claim's own digits. But a request can send a structured spec whose literal is not the number it claims, and nothing compares the two, so a false claim can earn a window it never stated. checker-36 measured this in the numeric and equality modes on archives of the code, at base and at 96b713e. It reaches every verifier that reads a literal this way. This run ties the window to the claim: a literal widens nothing unless it is the same number as the value claimed. It also closes band()'s float edge, where an overflowed window's upper edge can hold an infinite claim, and it makes every domain's memo fingerprint cover base.py, so these fixes reach stored verdicts. concordance-2 is filed to take the same rule in its own run.
